description: This line plot, titled “Ablation Study on HateXplain Dataset,” illustrates the performance of five model variants across three evaluation metrics—Precision, Recall, and F1-score—expressed as percentages. The x-axis, labeled “Model Variants,” is categorical and lists five configurations: “Full model (Ours),” “w/o Prompt,” “w/o Augmentation,” “w/o Attention,” and “w/o Prompt & Augmentation.” The y-axis, labeled “Metric (%)”, is linear, ranging from 56 to 66, with major gridlines at 58, 60, 62, 64, and 66. Three distinct lines represent the metrics: Precision (purple line with circular markers), Recall (light blue line with circular markers), and F1-score (brown line with circular markers). For the “Full model (Ours),” Precision is 65.44%, Recall is 65.56%, and F1-score is 65.49%. Removing the prompt causes all metrics to drop: Precision to 61.06%, Recall to 59.64%, and F1-score to 60.16%. Removing augmentation leads to Precision at 62.22%, Recall at 63.75%, and F1-score at 62.63%. Removing attention results in Precision rising to 64.06%, while Recall falls to 59.17% and F1-score to 59.67%. Finally, removing both prompt and augmentation yields Precision at 65.44%, Recall at 56.82%, and F1-score at 57.74%. The plot visually demonstrates how each component affects the model’s performance across different metrics.
